title: On-call hours consolidation — pre-announcement draft
content:
Purpose
- Draft for internal pre-announcement + talking points for the all-hands drop-in next week.
- Goal: explain why we are consolidating on-call windows, what stays the same, and customer risk mitigations.

High-level summary (one-line)
- We're moving to a consolidated follow-the-sun on-call schedule (4 overlapping regional shifts) to reduce handoff fatigue, lower alert duplication, and improve 24/7 coverage predictability. Nothing changes for customer-facing SLAs; this is an ops reorg to make responses more consistent.

Why now (bullet list for comms)
- On-call load uneven across regions and teams (data: median wakeups per week by region).
- Repeated handoff friction + duplicate alerts during overlap windows causing delayed mitigation.
- Hiring constraints: we can get better coverage by reorganizing shifts rather than increasing headcount immediately.
- Improves reliability for burst events (we can route escalations to nearest regional pod without noisy cross-queue paging).

What changes (practical)
- New schedule: 4 primary regional shifts (Americas, EMEA, APAC-1, APAC-2) with 1.5–2 hour engineered overlap windows for handoff and incident escalation.
- Single escalation matrix and runbook canonical source (Confluence link above).
- Engineers keep the same pager rotations within each pod; SRE leads will redistribute to balance load.
- Follow-the-sun ops Slack channel established; paging config updated to route based on local shift ownership first.

What does NOT change
- Customer SLAs and on-call response expectations remain unchanged.
- Support escalation policies remain intact.
- Everyone on-call still has the same incident severity definitions and postmortem obligations.

Risks & mitigations (for Q&A)
- Risk: perceived loss of ownership by product teams. Mitigation: we keep product-owner on-call handoff pairing during major incidents and maintain a secondary notification path.
- Risk: reduced overlap during rare cross-region incidents. Mitigation: temporary cross-region hotfix rotation during large-scale events; automatic fallback to global pager if regional capacity saturated.
- Risk: configuration mistakes. Mitigation: rollout a canary config to a small set of services for 2 weeks, monitor paging telemetry (SLOs: mean time to ack, mean time to resolve).

Rollout timeline (for comms)
- This week: pre-announce to SRE + leads (this doc).
- Week 1 (pilot): canary across 6 non-critical services (SRE-412 handles config change).
- Week 2–3: iterate on runbooks, adjust overlap windows based on metrics.
- Week 4: company-wide all-hands announcement + new schedule enforced.

All-hands talking points (short, for leader)
- Thank you to all on-call engineers — we know this is disruptive work.
- We are changing the schedule so fewer people get woken up multiple nights in a row and so handoffs are cleaner.
- No change to SLAs or customer commitments; this is purely internal ops optimization.
- If you have concerns, come to the ops drop-in on Thu 10:30 PT or DM me directly.

Email/Slack pre-announcement (draft)
- Subject: Heads-up: planned consolidation of on-call hours (pilot next week)
- Body: Hi team — we’re piloting a consolidated follow-the-sun on-call schedule to reduce handoff noise and improve response consistency. Pilot runs next week for 2 weeks on a handful of services. We will share measured outcomes and invite feedback at the Thu ops drop-in. Links: pilot runbook, feedback form.

Q&A (anticipated questions and short answers)
- Q: Will this increase my on-call burden?
  A: Overall no — shifts are rebalanced so most people will see fewer fragmented wakeups. If your team’s load increases we will rebalance.
- Q: Who do I escalate to if regional pod is overloaded?
  A: Built-in fallback to global on-call and SRE lead; see escalation matrix in runbook.
- Q: Is pay/comp changing for on-call?
  A: No changes to compensation; if coverage needs rise we will revisit resource plans.
- Q: How will we measure success?
  A: Primary metrics: mean time to acknowledge, mean time to resolve, and number of multi-region escalations. Also qualitative feedback via feedback form.

Open items / notes-to-self (actionable)
- Finalize canary service list with Ravi. (owner: Ravi)
- Update PagerDuty routing and test with synthetic alerts. (owner: Noor)
- Create feedback Google form + anonymize responses. (owner: Inez)
- Draft customer-facing note if pilot reveals any customer-visible risk. (owner: Rowan)
- Confirm overlap windows timezone math (double-check DST edge cases for APAC-2).

Meeting plan for Thu ops drop-in
- 10:30–10:35: quick framing by Amelia
- 10:35–10:50: SRE leads present pilot config and expected impact
- 10:50–11:10: Q&A and live-runbook walkthrough (show pager routing)
- 11:10–11:20: collect feedback, share form link, next steps

Tone guidance for announcement
- Empathetic — acknowledge on-call pain and tradeoffs.
- Data-driven — call out metrics we’ll track, not just gut.
- Reassuring — emphasize no SLA changes and iterative pilot.

Draft checklist before send
- [ ] Runbook link published and canonicalized
- [ ] PagerDuty test completed and logs inspected
- [ ] Canary services confirmed and owners notified
- [ ] Ops drop-in scheduled and calendar invites sent
- [ ] Feedback form live and shared in slide deck

Notes (informal)
- Keep email short — too many words = more Slack questions. Link to this doc for details.
- Consider a short Loom demo of new routing for the drop-in — helps reduce questions.

-- end of draft --

(Do not publish in current form; this is a working note. Will convert to polished all-hands slide and short Slack/email copy once pilot config is stable.)
